I wrote the suite in `tests/public/isIgnored.test.ts`. `tsc` builds it with no errors, and every test fails with `not implemented`, as expected. I deleted the `.js` files the build created in `src/` and `tests/public/`, so only the test file is new.

**The spec has no tagged scenarios.** `spec.md` is a single paragraph with no `@happy`/`@unhappy` tags. So the `[kind-N]` keys you asked for have nothing to point to, and I had to choose the keys myself. I treated each rule the spec lists as one scenario, in the spec's order, and keyed them all as `happy`:

| Key | Rule | Happy path | Boundary case |
|---|---|---|---|
| `[happy-1]` | glob patterns | `*.log` matches a file at any depth | in `doc/*.txt`, `*` doesn't cross `/` |
| `[happy-2]` | `#` comments | `#notes.txt` is a comment, not a pattern | `\#notes.txt` is a pattern that matches `#notes.txt` |
| `[happy-3]` | `!` re-include | `!keep.log` overrides an earlier `*.log` | it can't re-include a file whose parent directory is excluded |
| `[happy-4]` | trailing `/` | `build/` ignores everything under any `build` directory | `build/` doesn't match a file named `build` |
| `[happy-5]` | leading `/` | `/todo.txt` matches only at the root | a slash in the middle (`doc/frotz`) also anchors to the root |

If this suite is checked against a tagged version of the spec, the keys will need changing to match it.

The spec defines its rules only as "gitignore's usual ones", so I took each expected result from git's documented gitignore behaviour. I avoided less certain areas such as trailing spaces, `**`, and character classes.

10 tests, in 1 file.
